topic: Useful and Harmful Changes in Materials
key_concepts: Some material changes are useful, such as cutting cloth or wood into products.
Burning tires and plastics and dumping chemicals are harmful material changes.
Dumping garbage on land pollutes soil and creates pest breeding places.
Pests from polluted land carry germs that can cause disease.
Dumping garbage and factory chemical wastes into rivers pollutes water.
Drinking contaminated water can cause sickness and polluted water kills aquatic life.
Smoke, ashes, and dust from factories and vehicles pollute air.
Polluted air can cause skin itchiness, lung infections, cancer, and respiratory diseases.
Deforestation harms air quality, rainfall, soil, and animal habitats; reforestation helps.
The 5Rs of waste management are reduce, reuse, recycle, repair, and rot.
Biodegradable wastes can be composted; non-biodegradable wastes include plastics, rubber,
Waste segregation helps prevent or minimize harmful effects of burning garbage.
